questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The city
The climate
Culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Go on exchange!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult in the beginning, with a lot of practical things to be done.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Talked with KU and emailed with UB

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We actually just ended with finding an apartment on Airbnb, which was very easy. But we were also 4 people from home. Very recommended to try and find some people before exchange, and find an apartment with them.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Definitely worth it, not that interesting living on campus. Don't think people do it on UB.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Also a bit difficult but worth the work.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Emailing with UB was very easy and they are very quick to reply.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: You have to ready at a certain time when courses get up. But if you are just ready at that time it should be possible get the desired courses. I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready when it is possible to choose courses

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was fine. The level was kind of the same as at home. They are not that digital though, so all tests and so on are in paper. But didn't really bother

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar. Uses powerpoint in all classes

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International marketing
Culture and business in europe and western countries
Corporate Finance 
Global suistainability 
International markets and instruments

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
International marketing: Not that interesting and bad a teacher, but quite easy.
Culture and business in europe and western countries: Very chill subject but quite nice. Not that you learn that much, but highly recomended 
Corporate Finance: You learn quite a lot, and need to put in some work.
Global suistainability: Very easy subject as well, if you just want to enjoy Barcelona and not do much school. 
International markets and instruments: Also quite easy, but you learn a bit.

questions.answer: Got a fine for driving on a bike with headphones. 100 euro

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Alcohol on bars are super cheap
In general everything it is very cheap compared to Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
They have a sports club 5 minutes away from campus which is very much recommended. 120 euro for your whole stay and you can play paddle, tennis, football and go to the gym for free. 
You should at least do it for padel, so much fun.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Erasmus have a lot of things planned, just follow their instagram for Barcelona. Didn't use it that much though

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Play padel
Play street football in Barceloneta 
Invest in a beachvolley net and play it on the beach
Spikeball aswell on the beach
Drink beer and go to the many good night clubs they have down here especially Sutton and razzmatazz

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Eat tapas at perikete, get cava just nearby where there probably is a queue
Hike tibidabo, see sagrada, go to the beach, visit monjuic, go to night clubs.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I got into a football team with some locals from my classs, otherwise you don't really socialize that much with locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothinhg

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: All the activities happening all over the city at all time

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Just go
you avoid danish winter
get new friends for life

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Remember to explore the city 
Go on trips around spain in the weekend

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New friends and experiences

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having time to all the nice stuff Barcelona have to offer

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
